newsitem.title: USA: Cloudy skies delay shuttle landing.
newsitem.headline: Cloudy skies delay shuttle landing.

text.p: Flight controllers ordered shuttle Discovery to stay aloft for another orbit of earth on Friday after cloudy skies ruined its first landing attempt in Florida.
The shuttle, which was nearing the end of a 10-day mission to refurbish the Hubble Space Telescope, had a second opportunity to land at the Kennedy Space Centre at 3:32 a.m. EST (0832 GMT).

Mission control called off Discovery's planned 1:50 a.m. EST (0650 GMT) touchdown after a weather reconnaissance plane noticed clouds "popping up around" the shuttle's 15,000-foot (4,572 metre) -long runway.
"We're going to have to wave off," mission control's Kevin Kregel informed the crew. "We had some low clouds formed up into a broken layer. Hopefully they will dissipate."
Forecasters were looking at the weather for the second opportunity in Florida and also at the backup landing strip at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
The conditions in Florida were expected to remain uncertain while weather at the west coast runway was "fairly good," he said.
Discovery's planned nighttime landing would be only the ninth in the 82-flight shuttle programme.
The shuttle, running low on electrical power and other supplies, was expected to land by Saturday at the latest, Hale had earlier said.

Discovery blasted off from the Kennedy Space Centre before dawn on Feb. 11. Two teams of spacewalking astronauts spent 33 hours outside to refurbish and upgrade the $2 billion orbiting observatory. They installed two new instruments and eight other upgraded compartments.
